objective: Prove, for the cut-open torus walk at n = 2^m, h = n/2: (1) the return map C_s of CONE-COLLAPSE-20261109-001A is w^(n+1) T_h(w^-2), where T_h(c) is the matrix, in the basis W_k(t + 1/t) = sum_(|j|<=k) t^j (k < h) of F[c][K]/(K^h), of f -> (K + c)(iota f)(K + c) mod K^h, iota(W_k) = W_(h-1-k); (2) T_1 = [c] and T_2h = P [[A(R + c^h), c^h AR], [A + u(c^h u + v)^T, AR + c^h u v^T]] P with A = T_h, R the reversal, u = e_0, v = e_(h-1), P = [[I, R], [0, I]]; (3) the operator without the reversal, S_h = T_h R, has det(zI + S_h) = c^h (1 + sum_(j<m) (z/c)^(2^j)): its eigenvalues are c x for the h elements x of GF(n) of trace 1; (4) the target: every nonzero root of det(lambda^(n+1) I + T_h(lambda^2)) is a (2n - 1)-th root of unity, at every power of two, or the gap stated.
status: Proved 2026-11-09 (by hand, with finite checks; pre-registered in aaa3e7be3): at n = 2^m the cut-open torus's return map is one-dimensional, C_s = w^(n+1) T_h(w^-2) on F[K]/(K^h) in the ball basis; its reversal is multiplication by the involution eps = W_(h-1) = 1 + sum_j K^(h - h/2^j); without the reversal the eigenvalues are c times the trace-1 elements of GF(n); the digit recursion builds S_2h and eps_2h from S_h and eps_h (two-by-two blocks, from T_1 = [c]), with det(zI + T_2h) = det(z^2 + S_h^2 + c^h z (eps_h S_h + E)); and the cone polynomial is a linearized determinant, det(I - mu A_cone) = mu^(-h) det(sum_(i=0..m) mu^(2^i) C_i), C_0 = S^-1, C_i = N^(h - 2^(i-1)), C_m = I, the shape of the trace of GF(2n). Computed: 1 + Tr_(GF(2n)) divides the cone polynomial exactly once with a square quotient (sides 4 to 32; 64 in the stress run). The registered target, the collapse at every power of two, is not proved: it is now the statement that the linearized determinant's roots lie in GF(2n).
title: A one-dimensional return map and its digit recursion
